candidates.name: Atrial Tachycardia
support_spans: A 12-lead ECG during tachycardia showed an atrial cycle length of 280 ms with positive P waves in leads II, III, aVF, and V₁
candidates.why: The patient presented with palpitations and had a history of atrial fibrillation, suggesting a possible arrhythmia.

candidates.name: Mitral Isthmus Dependent Atrial Flutter
support_spans: An electroanatomic activation map demonstrated counterclockwise propagation around the mitral annulus and left atrial appendage, interrupted by a low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line
contradict_spans: a postpacing interval more than 20 ms longer than the cycle length when pacing adjacent to the mitral isthmus scar
candidates.why: The electroanatomic activation map showed counterclockwise propagation around the mitral annulus, consistent with mitral isthmus dependent atrial flutter.

candidates.name: Epicardial Accessory Pathway Mediated Tachycardia
support_spans: These findings suggested an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar
recordings showed activation within the vein of Marshall that matched the tachycardia cycle length
candidates.why: The findings suggested an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar, and the recordings in the vein of Marshall matched the tachycardia cycle length.

candidates.name: Atrial Tachycardia due to Epicardial Accessory Pathway
support_spans: entrainment pacing revealed postpacing intervals within 20 ms of the tachycardia cycle length at the inferior and lateral mitral annulus and at the left atrial appendage–left pulmonary vein ridge
contradict_spans: interrupted by a low-voltage scar at the prior mitral isthmus line
candidates.why: The patient's history of prior catheter ablations and the presence of a low-voltage scar at the mitral isthmus line suggest a complex atrial substrate, and the entrainment pacing results indicate an epicardial pathway bypassing the scar.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because it represents a rare and complex cause of atrial tachycardia that may be easily missed by a 'common disease first' approach.
